sections.heading: Box truck lettering or a full wrap — which one do you actually need?
sections.body: Most commercial trucks do not need a full wrap. If the box is already a usable color, cut vinyl lettering puts the company name, phone number and logo on it for a fraction of the printed film. A full wrap is for artwork that has to cover the panel. Applied Graphics in Kenilworth, NJ does all four options below, so the recommendation is not driven by what they happen to sell.

Beyond New Jersey, they cover New York, Philadelphia, Connecticut and Boston, and work through a national installer network for fleets outside that radius.

sections.body: Because the warranty is not available otherwise. Only graphics manufacturers holding a current Certificate of 3M MCS Warranty may extend it. Every installer at Applied Graphics is 3M-certified, and the company is independently listed in the UASG directory as a 3M Certified Graphics Installer — third-party corroboration, not a self-claim. Their own line: "We are CERTIFIED and that makes all the difference. Don't waste your money on wraps that don't have a warranty!"
